entries.title: Method Switch
entries.short: The system recommends a different method when you stagnate - you decide whether to switch.
entries.long:
## What is the method switch?

If your learning stagnates in a method while it causes
high stress, Adaptive Learner suggests a method switch.
You see the suggestion as a banner above the session
chat and can accept or dismiss it.

## When the suggestion fires

The rule looks at your last three session ratings. Both
conditions must hold:

- **No progress in understanding**: the three
  understanding scores do not rise (the same score three
  times counts as stagnant).
- **Average stress above 3** (on the 1-5 scale) across
  the same three ratings.

With fewer than three ratings there is no suggestion. A
difficult phase that still shows progress, or stagnation
without stress, does not trigger it.

## Which method is suggested

The method with the highest weight in your learning
profile that you have not used recently. Without a
profile, the next method in the fixed method order.

## You decide

The system recommends; you choose. Accepting switches
the session and records a ``MethodSwitch`` entry (a
trail for your profile). Dismissing hides the suggestion
for the rest of this session; the next session checks
again.

## Why not automatic?

Method switches are a big change in the learning
experience. An automatic switch would break learning
continuity and could fire during a difficult but
productive phase. You know your context better than the
system does.

entries.title: Auto-Loop
entries.short: After step 7, a new cycle with fresh content starts automatically.
entries.long:
## What is the auto-loop?

When you complete step 7 (integrate), the session can
automatically start a new cycle on the next topic from
your curriculum — without you pressing a "next cycle"
button.

## How the next topic is chosen

- **If a curriculum exists**: the next topic in the
  hierarchical order.
- **If no curriculum exists**: the AI generates a
  suitable follow-up topic based on the current
  trajectory.
- **If spaced-repetition cards are due**: they are
  prioritized before new content.

## Cycle counter

Every session shows a cycle counter ("3/5"). When
max_cycles is reached (default: 5), auto-loop pauses
and asks whether you want to continue. This protects
against runaway sessions.

## How to interrupt the auto-loop

- **Submit a rating**: after each cycle, you get the
  three sliders (understanding, stress, method fit). If
  stress > 3, the system suggests a break.
- **"End session" button**: clickable at any time.
- **Accept a method switch**: breaks the current loop
  and starts a new one with the new method.

## When auto-loop is most valuable

For language learning with small topic units, where
"start a new session" overhead slows learning down. For
coding, auto-loop is often less useful because topic
transitions are larger.

entries.title: Spaced Repetition
entries.short: Time-optimized review based on your learning history.
entries.long:
## What is spaced repetition?

Spaced repetition is the technique of placing reviews at
increasing intervals. It uses the forgetting-curve
effect: each successfully recalled item lasts longer
next time.

## The bands in Adaptive Learner

Every exercise element you answer is tracked. The next
review date depends on how often in a row you answered
it correctly:

- **0 correct in a row** (or just answered wrong):
  review 1 day later.
- **1 correct in a row**: 3 days later.
- **2 or more correct in a row**: 7 days later.

At **3 correct answers in a row** the element counts as
mastered and leaves the review queue. A later wrong
answer brings it back.

## What shifts the date

- **Hint used**: the interval is halved, because the
  answer came with help.
- **Correct in Exam mode**: the interval is doubled,
  because an answer without help is stronger evidence.

## When the system recommends reviews

When elements are due, a review card appears on the
Dashboard with the number of due and overdue elements
and an **Open review session** button. Overdue elements come
first, then those with the most errors. Details: see the
lessons guide.

entries.title: Conversation Analysis / Import
entries.short: Analyze existing chat histories and extract concrete learning artifacts from them.
entries.long:
## What is conversation analysis?

Adaptive Learner can analyze existing chats from
ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini and extract learning content
from them. You import the transcript once — the system
reads it, structures it, and turns it into a usable
learning artifact.

## What gets extracted

- **Concepts** — terms and ideas discussed in the chat.
- **Knowledge gaps** — points where you asked follow-ups
  or made mistakes.
- **Errors** — concrete misconceptions visible in the
  chat.
- **Vocabulary / terminology** — domain words
  (especially relevant for language learning or
  specialized fields).

## How the import works

1. Export your chat from ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini as
  Markdown or JSON.
2. Upload the file into Adaptive Learner (drag-and-drop
  or file picker).
3. The system detects the format automatically and
  stores the messages.
4. Trigger the analysis — the AI reads the chat in your
  learning language and produces the structured
  breakdown.

## What you can do next

Three actions follow from the analysis:

- **"Create curriculum"** — the extracted concepts feed
  into a hierarchical curriculum.
- **"Start session"** — a session that starts directly
  from the detected knowledge gaps.
- **"Generate Anki cards"** — flashcards from the
  concepts and vocabulary.

## Duplicates

If you import the same chat twice, the system detects it
via the content hash and offers to navigate to the
existing analysis instead of creating a copy.

## Privacy

Chat contents go ONLY to your active AI provider (the
one you configured in settings). The system sends
nothing to a central server. When you delete the chat,
the contents are gone.

entries.title: Gamification (XP, Badges, Streaks)
entries.short: Progress system with experience points, badges and streaks - motivation without gimmickry.
entries.long:
## What is the gamification layer?

Three mechanics make learning progress visible and
rewarding:

- **XP (experience points)** - for completed sessions
  and lessons, the assessment and conversation imports.
  Levels rise with XP.
- **Badges** - for milestones (first session, staying
  consistent, trying methods, depth, several languages).
- **Streaks** - consecutive days with learning activity.

## How XP is earned

- **Completed session**: 50 XP, +10 XP per completed
  cycle, +25 XP per cycle that reached step 7.
- **First session in a new method**: +50 XP.
- **Completed lesson**: 30 XP, +10 XP per star, +20 XP
  for three stars with every step right on the first
  attempt.
- **Streak multiplier**: +25% per streak day on session
  and lesson XP, up to 7 days (at most 2.75x).
- **Game mode combo**: up to 20 extra XP for a lesson
  played with combos.
- **Assessment completed**: 100 XP.
- **Conversation imported and analysed**: 75 XP.

Levels grow on a widening curve: level 2 at 100 XP,
level 3 at 300, level 4 at 600, level 5 at 1000 - each
gap is 100 XP larger than the one before.

## Badges are not coercive

You do *not* need a single badge to use the app
productively. They are a mirror, not a target. Badge
notifications can be turned off in settings.

## Streak freezes

Every 7 streak days earn one streak freeze, up to 3 in
stock. If you miss a day, a freeze is used automatically
and pauses your streak instead of resetting it. With
weekend mode on, Saturday and Sunday do not count as
gaps.

## Why this works without gimmicks

Learning research shows: extrinsic reward can destroy
intrinsic motivation ("overjustification effect").
Adaptive Learner relies on the mechanics being a
**mirror** of progress, not an incentive system. No
leaderboards, no social features, no point-sharing -
the data stays with you.

## Reset

If the gamification values no longer match your
situation (e.g. fresh start after a long break), you
can reset XP, badges and streak in settings. Curriculum,
sessions, and ratings are preserved.

entries.title: Dashboard
entries.short: Your home base: progress, streak, XP, badges, due reviews, and quick actions.
entries.long:
## What does the dashboard show?

The dashboard is your command center. "Continue learning"
sits at the top with your most recently touched lesson,
then the actionable cards (paused lessons, missions, focus
areas, review queue), then gamification (XP, streak,
badges), and finally the analytical panels.

## Filter

A subject filter lists only your own subjects, sorted by
most-used first.

entries.title: Content browser
entries.short: The page where you find, download, and start lesson sets.
entries.long:
## How do I find lessons?

The content browser at /content is built around the
learning flow: search first (instant, accent-tolerant),
then "Continue learning", then the catalogue. The catalogue
splits into "Languages" (source > target > level) and
"Knowledge" (non-language domains).

## Sources and books

Source badges show where a set comes from; a source filter
hides individual sources. A domain can surface book
recommendations.

entries.title: Lesson
entries.short: The viewer that walks you step by step through a lesson's theory and exercises.
entries.long:
## How do the exercises work?

A lesson is a sequence of theory and exercise steps.
Every set can use the core exercise types (matching,
picture choice, free text, cloze, word tiles, multiple
choice); some sets add further types such as
categorization or audio dictation. The full list is in
the features overview.

## Controls

Enter checks an answered exercise and advances. From an
exercise you can jump to the matching theory via "Re-read
theory". At the end you see your score with stars and can
export it as Markdown.

entries.title: Settings
entries.short: Everything you can change without code or YAML - language, AI, learning, data, appearance.
entries.long:
## What can I configure?

Settings bundle language, AI provider and keys, storage
mode, learning options (e.g. Enter shortcut, preferred
exercise direction), data (backup, content repositories),
appearance (12 themes), and gamification.

## Your data in your hands

Under "Data" you create and import backups and connect your
own content repositories. None of it leaves your device
unasked.

entries.title: Backup and restore
entries.short: A complete snapshot of your learning state that you can save and restore elsewhere.
entries.long:
## What is a backup?

A backup is a complete snapshot: every data table
(projects, sessions, lesson progress, errors,
gamification, missions ...), your downloaded content
sets and your local preferences - bundled into one
``.alb`` file (a ZIP archive). Older single-JSON backups
still import.

## Cross-identity

You can import a backup into a fresh installation or under
a different profile; the restore re-resolves internal
references cleanly. On import you see a per-table summary.
